title: France Making An Even Bigger Mess of Its Cannabis Policy, But Finally About to Legalize Medical After Only Thirty Years

content_html_sanitized:
My first visit to Paris was about thirty years ago when I went with a Dutch friend who was an expert on international law, especially regarding the EU and cannabis.


He was there as a consultant to the defense attorney, the late Francis Caballero,  who was also a professor at Paris Nanterre University. He was accompanied by several of his students, who were some of the most beautiful women I have ever seen. Vive la France!


The French legal system is different from the Anglo Saxon model. It does not have a jury system, but trials are held before a panel of judges, and there is a constitutional requirement for the presumption of innocence. 


However, in this case, there was no doubt about the defendant having cannabis, but there was also no doubt about him having a medical condition that doctors said responded only to cannabis. 


The only question was whether French law provided a medical necessity defense.


My high school French had long since faded away, (Sorry, Ms Welles), but the long term answer was Non, but the shorter answer was to find a loophole that avoided jailing an obviously sick man.


Now, thirty years later, France still does not have a medical cannabis law.  


However, as of March 2022, it does have a loophole for cultivating medical cannabis.

See France Legalizes Medical Cannabis Cultivation 


And, finally, as of March 20th of this year, “France makes key move towards legalising medical cannabis.” 

“In 2023, lawmakers had voted to approve the sale of medical cannabis products for a five-year period, but the law was never acted because it required the Health Ministry to send it to the European Commission. After months of uncertainty – and political chaos, with eight health ministers have been appointed since the start of the experiment in 2021 – the process is once again moving forward.”


How time flies…


But…. “It could take several months for experts at the European Commission to finally approve the regulations, and then the French high health authority (HAS) will need to rule on how medical cannabis could eventually be covered by the public health insurance.” 


Of course, it didn’t have to be this way.

See France forgets own golden age of medical marijuana


And from 1998, seePressure Grows in France for Medical Cannabis and a General Reform of Cannabis Laws


Yep, marijuana prohibition causes long term memory loss.


In the meantime, the very mean time, the recreational cannabis laws are an absurd mess, and are probably about to get worse.


According to Forensic Science International, “A study of cannabis potency in France over a 25 years period (1992–2016)” “Europe is one of the world’s largest consumer markets for cannabis resin, yet the market in Western Europe may now be dominated by herbal cannabis [2], [3].


In France, cannabis is by far the most seized and consumed illicit drug [4].


However, contrary to many other European countries, it is the resin type, commonly known as hashish, which is the most popular form, even if local cultivation and consumption of herbal cannabis, i.e. marijuana, has been increasing for the last three years.”


As for potency: “The increased potency of both herbal and resin cannabis in France is proved through the monitoring of THC content. For cannabis resin, it has slowly risen from 1992 to 2009, before a considerable increase in the last four years (mean THC content in mid-2016 is 23% compared to 10% in 2009). For herbal cannabis, it has known three main stages of growth (mean THC content is 13% in 2015 and mid-2016 compared to 7% in 2009 and 2% in 1995). The calculation of THC/CBD ratios in both herbal and resin samples confirms the recent change in chemotypes in favor of high potency categories. Finally, the CBN/THC ratios in marijuana samples were measured in order to evaluate the freshness of French seized hemp.”


So, doesn’t this prove that hashish is much stronger than it used to be, so it has to remain illegal? Glad you asked.


Non. 


First, almost all of the hash seized in France is smuggled from North Africa or the Middle East, and the economics of contraband actually encourages greater potency of whatever it is. 

See The Iron Law of Prohibition https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_law_of_prohibition 


Second, it is almost impossible for the consumer to determine the potency of most hash, contraband or not, so it is even more important to legalize hash than herbal cannabis. 


But that is not the direction that things are going in France. Au contraire, Pierre.

From Politico Europe:France looks to toughen war on drugs strategy amid trafficking surge. Ministers are looking to crack down on drug dealing networks and are pushing back against calls for legalization…


“Since 2021, France has opted for a model based on hitting drug users with a minimum fine that does not require prosecution in order to disincentivize consumption. In February, the Interior Ministry boasted that 288,000 people had been sanctioned for their consumption, a 10 percent year-on-year increase.”


It doesn’t seem to be working: “According to the French Observatory on Drugs and Addictive Behaviors, cannabis is the most popular illicit drug in France, followed by cocaine and ecstasy/MDMA.


While some French lawmakers have floated decriminalization and the legalization of cannabis — France is the European Union's third-highest consumer of weed behind Czechia and Italy — they remain in the minority.


“In February, Retailleau borrowed Darmanin's saying that "a joint has the taste of blood," directly attributing the responsibility for trafficking-related murders to people who buy cannabis.”


But not to the people who pass stupid laws???


And remember that this December 17 will be the fiftieth anniversary of the first Coffee Shop in Amsterdam.

SeeCrime comparison between France and The Netherlands

AndCrime comparison between Amsterdam and Paris 

 

Or Problem with people using or dealing drugs: 

Amsterdam Low 37.89 

Paris High 64.87


And finally, the French government cannot even control its prisons.

See “French prisons hit by wave of attacks after clampdown on drug traffickers. Terrorism office launches investigation into assaults including gunmen opening fire on entrance to Toulon jail.”


So the French politicians want to waste more money and finite law enforcement resources on cannabis prohibition, and subsidize the gangs by keeping cannabis in the black market??
